title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Amount of the Final Detention Line
content:
## Definition

The amount of a Demurrage and Detention Free Time record's final detention line is the sum of the detention day rates of all the detention days the line bills, each day at the rate for its own slab and rate class. No dangerous-goods uplift is ever applied to a detention day, whatever cargo the booking carries. Rounding happens once, on the finished total of the day rates; the rates of individual days are not rounded.

## Same definition, grouped by slab

The amount equals the days in slab 1 multiplied by the slab 1 detention rate, together with the days in slab 2 multiplied by the slab 2 rate, the days in slab 3 multiplied by the slab 3 rate and the days in slab 4 multiplied by the slab 4 rate, all four products added and the total then rounded to the cent.

## Worked illustration (hypothetical rates)

Suppose detention rates of 50.00, 84.00, 124.00 and 170.00 for slabs 1 to 4, and a line billing 4 days in slab 1, 4 in slab 2 and 1 in slab 3.

- Slab 1: 4 days at 50.00 comes to 200.00.
- Slab 2: 4 days at 84.00 comes to 336.00.
- Slab 3: 1 day at 124.00 comes to 124.00.
- Line amount: 660.00.

If the same container moved under a dangerous-goods booking, the line amount would still be 660.00, since the uplift never reaches detention days.
